title: Out of Sight, Not Out of Clues: Can Video LLMs Guess from Partial Evidence?
abstract: arXiv:2611.34126v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: In real-world applications like egocentric recording, visual accessibility, and surveillance review, visual evidence for Video Large Language Models (Video LLMs) is often only partially captured. A reliable model should match its response to the evidence: answering when sufficient, guessing from visible clues when partial, and abstaining when absent. Yet existing benchmarks enforce a binary answerable-or-unanswerable split, leaving partial evidence unmeasured and obscuring whether failures arise from missing evidence or misjudging sufficiency. We introduce ClueProbe, a diagnostic benchmark to (1) separate perceiving evidence from judging sufficiency, and (2) validate our diagnosis via targeted fine-tuning. ClueProbe comprises 1,721 human-annotated questions across 598 natural videos, labeled Answerable, Guessable, or Unanswerable, alongside controlled perturbations altering wording or visual input. translated_title: 看不见，但线索犹存：视频大语言模型能从部分证据中进行猜测吗？
translated_abstract: 在自我中心录像、视觉无障碍辅助、监控审查等现实应用中，视频大语言模型所获得的视觉证据往往只是部分被捕捉到的。一个可靠的模型应当使回应与证据相匹配：证据充分时作答，证据部分可见时基于可见线索进行猜测，证据缺失时选择拒答。然而，现有基准强制采用“可回答或不可回答”的二元划分，使得部分证据情形未被测量，也掩盖了模型的失败究竟源于证据缺失还是对证据充分性的误判。我们提出了ClueProbe，一个诊断性基准，旨在：（1）将证据感知能力与充分性判断能力分离；（2）通过针对性微调来验证我们的诊断。ClueProbe包含基于598个自然视频的1,721个经人工标注的问题，标记为“可回答”、“可猜测”或“不可回答”，并配合改变措辞或视觉输入的受控扰动。我们对10个开源及专有模型进行了评估……
tldr: 提出诊断基准ClueProbe，通过将问题划分为“可回答、可猜测、不可回答”三类，把视频大语言模型的证据感知能力与证据充分性判断能力解耦，揭示其在部分证据下的猜测能力缺陷，并借助针对性微调验证了诊断结论。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces ClueProbe, a diagnostic benchmark that separates evidence perception from sufficiency judgment for Video LLMs by labeling questions as Answerable, Guessable, or Unanswerable, exposing how models guess from partial visual evidence and validating the diagnosis through targeted fine-tuning.
